item.title: The whistleblower, the Forest Service, and an endless battle in North Carolina’s mountains
item.description: For decades, the Forest Service has relied on a probability model that suggests most such artifacts will be found in relatively flat areas. This rule of thumb has left steeper slopes, which make up the vast majority of North Carolina’s national forests, largely uninterrogated in any formal sense.
